      • CalculateMappingOfRoots

        public static long[] CalculateMappingOfRoots(long n)
        To make rotations of slots work, the roots of unity need to be in a particular order, and the substitutions that must happen for the a given rotation have to correspond to that order. This function returns an ordering of the powers of the generator of the group that gives the right pattern of rotations. There is probably some very nice sophisticated (or simple!) bit of maths to make this happen, but I don't know it (yet).
        Parameters:
        n - number of elements in the encoding
        Returns:
        an array of the power the generator must be raised to

      • CalculateRootsOfUnity

        public static long[] CalculateRootsOfUnity(long n,
                                           long t)
        Calculates a k such that k^2n mod t == 1 and where k^i mod t != 1 for all i != 2n Then the other roots of unity are k^(2i+1) mod t, i from 0 to n-1 Cool fact: Prod(i=0)(i=n-1) (x-k^(2i+1)) = x^n + 1 mod t
        Parameters:
        n - subgroup size
        t - prime and congruent to 1 mod 2n
        Returns:

      • CalculateBasisFunctions

        public static UnivariatePolynomialZp64[] CalculateBasisFunctions(long n,
                                                                 long t,
                                                                 long[] rootsOfUnity)
        Calculate the polynomials that allow projections into and out of the slots in the plaintext. They are a set of polynomials, b_j(x) such that if we call the roots of unity a_i, then b_j(a_i) = \delta_{ij} - that is, if you evaluate the polynomials at the roots of unity, they are 1 for only their corresponding polynomial and zero otherwise. To encode a message v_i we write m(x) = Sum_i v_i b_i(x) And the components of the message can be obtained from v_i = m(a_i)
        Parameters:
        n - number of slots
        t - prime and congruent to 1 mod 2n
        rootsOfUnity - precalculated roots of unity for n and t
        Returns:

      • generateNoisePolynomial

        public static UnivariatePolynomialZp64 generateNoisePolynomial(long n,
                                                               long t,
                                                               double sigma,
                                                               double sigmamax)
        Generate a polynomial with n coefficients (i.e. order n-1) which are numbers modulo t. The distribution of these coefficients is a truncated gaussian with variance sigma and cutoff sigmamax.
        Parameters:
        n - number of coefficients
        t - modulus of coefficients
        sigma - variance of distribution
        sigmamax - cutoff of distribution
        Returns:
        polynomial with noise ceofficients

      • dotProducWithPowers

        public static UnivariatePolynomialZp64 dotProducWithPowers(<any> field,
                                                           java.util.ArrayList<UnivariatePolynomialZp64> parray,
                                                           UnivariatePolynomialZp64 atom)
        Return a polynomial with the accumulated dot product of an array of polynomials with powers of a given polynomials. All operations should be done in the finite field given. This is a key step in the FV decryption process. [Sum parray_i atom^i] mod q mod x^n + 1
        Parameters:
        field - field under which the operations are to be performed
        parray - array of polynomials
        atom - polynomial which will have powers calculated
        Returns:
        polynomial with sum

      • multiplyPolyArraysDivideAndRound

        public static java.util.ArrayList<UnivariatePolynomialZp64> multiplyPolyArraysDivideAndRound(<any> field,
                                                                                             java.util.ArrayList<UnivariatePolynomialZp64> polys1,
                                                                                             java.util.ArrayList<UnivariatePolynomialZp64> polys2,
                                                                                             long scale)
        Implements the basic algorithm for FV ciphertext multiplication. This must be done in a very particular way to give correct results. The two polynomial arrays are multiplied as if they are polynomials in the secret key, this results in another array of polynomials with more elements. The coefficients of tehse are then divided by a scale, then the resulting polynomials are reduced modulo the quotient polynomial and ring modulus.
        Parameters:
        field - The field of the final polynomial
        polys1 - first array of polynomials
        polys2 - second array of polynomials
        scale - amount to divide product by
        Returns:
        array of polynomails
